newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Jospin seeks broadcasting law changes.
newsitem.headline: France's Jospin seeks broadcasting law changes.

text.p: French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said he will seek changes to the broadcasting law to guarantee a strong public television service, to strengthen broadcasting watchdog Le Conseil Superieur de l'Audiovisuel (CSA), and to establish mechanisms to counter media ownership concentration.
In his first policy speech since taking office at the beginning of this month, Jospin said public television needs to be able to compete with growing programme offerings.

"In television, backing pluralism means encouraging and supporting a strong, high-quality public service, which implies a change in the current share of public resources and advertising receipts," Jospin said.
He said the press had become vulnerable due to advertising moving to other media, and he said encouraging pluralism of the press meant adapting the regime of public aid.

"The imperative of independance is the corollary of freedom of communication. Independance is the guarantee given to journalists to exercise their trade, and to newsrooms rather than to shareholders," he said.

Jospin said the socialist government would defend "the cultural exception", which stands for France's desire to promote the French language and counter the hegemony of the United States in modern popular culture.
He said under the previous centre-right government the state's culture budget had fallen to well below one percent of total spending.
"The aim of this government is to reverse resolutely this trend and progressively achieve setting aside one percent of the state budget for culture," he said. DT/SLA
